e-8050.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
e-8050.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 2 & 2 & -8 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_i:=R_i+kR_1,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
e-8050.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below $a_{11}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 2 & 2 & -8 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & 10 & -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\qquad$ $R_2:=R_2-2R_1\quad$ and $\quad R_3:=R_3+3R_1.$

each of the form $R_i:=R_i+kR_2,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
e-8048.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below $a_{22}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\qquad$ $R_1 := R_1 - 2R_2\quad$ and $\quad R_4:=R_4+2R_2.$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{23}=-3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}.$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{23}=-3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}.$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}.$

content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}.$

decision.explanation: Subtract twice row 3 from each of rows 1 and 2: (-3,2,-1) - (0,2,4) = (-3,0,-5), and (1,2,1) - (0,2,4) = (1,0,-3). Row 3 stays unchanged, producing B.

after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & 2 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ 9 & 0 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
